known_incidents.resolution: An earlier BATCH3_BLOCKED_AREA2_SOURCE_EXHAUSTION verdict assumed one viable decision family yields at most one final-bank question. The schema requires max_questions_in_final_bank per family as an integer with minimum 1, and the distribution across 364 families is 26 at cap 1, 250 at cap 2, 88 at cap 3. validate_family_matrix errors only when released_count exceeds the cap. Global capacity and per-mock repetition are different things. The verdict was withdrawn via FEASIBILITY_CORRECTION_1 and the original artifact retained.
known_incidents.do_not_repeat: Do not re-derive an Area-2 exhaustion conclusion from family counts. Count question slots.

Seven items were converted from four-correct to three-correct. scripts/check_tranche_key_patterns.py now errors on count omission and warns on slot concentration.

known_incidents.resolution: Two confirmed citation defects were found: FED-PSE-QUANTITY cites 21 CFR 1314.20 for the 9 g/30-day limit, which that section does not contain (it is 21 U.S.C. 844(a); 1314.20(b)'s only 30-day figure is 7.5 g for mobile retail vendors), and MA-PMP-REPORTING pinpoints 105 CMR 700.012(C)(7) for the additional-drug power which is at (C)(8). Both were applied, scripts/update_content_hashes.py was run as validate_all directs, and validate_all went from 0 to 82 errors: 62 drug records pin those rules through verified_rule_dependencies, and released questions pin the drugs through final_adjudication.verified_dependencies. Re-pinning would have meant the controller silently re-adjudicating released questions against dependency content it had just changed. The change was reverted and the findings recorded in audits/controller/B3S3-V2-AUDITOR-SIDE-FINDINGS-VERIFICATION.json.
known_incidents.do_not_repeat: Do not casually re-apply these. The correction needs an independent re-adjudication of the roughly 13 released questions whose pins break. Neither defect changes any answer.

known_incidents.resolution: CLAUDE-FRESH-B3S3-V2 reported that MA-Q-0014's patient-requested partial fill 12 days after issue cannot satisfy a 5-day requirement in M.G.L. c. 94C s. 18(d3/4). Reading the statute, that five-day limit reaches only a prescription filled pursuant to subsection (d) or (d1/2), which are the out-of-state prescriber pathways: (d) covers a nonnarcotic Schedule II prescription issued by an out-of-state practitioner and (d1/2) a narcotic Schedule II prescription from a practitioner registered in Maine or a contiguous state. MA-Q-0014 is an ordinary in-state prescription, so the 30-day issue-date deadline governs, which is what it keys.
known_incidents.do_not_repeat: Do not treat this as a released-item defect without new evidence. MA-Q-0014 is AUDIT_PENDING in any case.

known_incidents.resolution: CLAUDE-FRESH-B3E-V3 measured that across the 234 SBA items outside its tranche the longest option is the key 153 times, 65.4%, against a 20% chance baseline. Choosing the longest option would score about 65% with no legal knowledge. The existing SBA_ANSWER_LENGTH_LEAKAGE detector misses it because it tests per-item outliers (a 1.6x ratio and a 6-token delta), not the aggregate tendency. The B3-E tranche itself measured 47.4%, better but still above chance. This controller did NOT independently verify the figure before the handoff freeze.
known_incidents.do_not_repeat: Verify the measurement first. If it holds it is a bank-wide exploitable pattern affecting released content and is arguably the most consequential open finding in this handoff, but it is not a Batch-3 completion blocker under the current gate set. Consider an aggregate length-bias detector alongside the per-item one.
